observation.visible_scene: Open ocean under a clear pale sky, with multiple breaking wave lines and white foam. In the first short segment two people in dark wetsuits are near the shore break: one stands crouched on a board inside the whitewater while another, closer to camera, holds a white surfboard painted with teal and red panels. After an abrupt editing cut the view widens to a line-up of several surfers: one in dark wetsuit paddles prone on a board in the mid-distance, others sit or float on boards in the foreground foam (a person with a white board at left, a seated person mid-left, a prone paddler, and a seated person at right).
visible_changes: An editing cut occurs between the first and second segments: the composition, wave pattern and number/arrangement of people change discontinuously, so the two views are not continuous physical motion.
After the cut, the mid-distance surfer transitions from lying prone on the board to a kneeling/popping-up posture (around frames 11-13) and then to standing on the board in a riding stance.

The standing surfer rides the breaking wave toward the camera, growing larger in frame and shifting from center-left toward center as the wave carries them shoreward, maintaining balance with arms outstretched through the rest of the segment.

The foreground surfers remain largely stationary, only bobbing and drifting slightly with the foam; the left surfer with the white board, the mid-left seated person and the right seated person keep roughly the same horizontal positions throughout.
The white foam lines advance toward the bottom of the frame (shoreward), and the crest the main surfer rides moves and breaks progressively lower in the scene.
In the pre-cut segment the standing surfer holds a crouched pose with little net movement, while the board-holding surfer stays upright in shallow water.
outside_clip_unknowns: What caused the cut between the two segments and whether they depict the same wave or different moments.
The outcome of the ride after the final frame (whether the surfer completes the wave or falls).
How the riding surfer caught the wave before the cut, since the takeoff is not shown.
The exact number of people and their activities outside the cropped time window.
uncertain_details: Whether the apparent approach of the riding surfer is due to the wave carrying them toward a fixed camera, a camera zoom, or a slight camera pan; background horizon evidence is too sparse to separate object motion from camera motion confidently.
Whether the striped board and the board ridden after the cut are the same board, given the discontinuity.
Precise identities and ages of the surfers; only dark wetsuits and light-colored boards are visible.

Both ends are arbitrary crop boundaries, not the beginning and completion of an action. Motion
may already be underway in the first view and may continue beyond the last. The endpoints need
NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
Return JSON {"visible_scene":"...", "visible_changes":["observation supported within the excerpt"],
"outside_clip_unknowns":["unseen prerequisites or outcomes, only when relevant"],
"uncertain_details":["..."]}. Be concrete and concise, in English. This is not a complete event reconstruction.
